study type: multimethod study (human-centred design and health care administrative data analysis)
exposure: Antimicrobial prophylaxis practices for early-onset neonatal group B Streptococcus (GBS) disease prevention
Antimicrobial prophylaxis practices for surgical site infection (SSI) prevention during labour and delivery
cohort: The study involved seven obstetrical healthcare providers for journey mapping and 13,818 patients who delivered in Alberta hospital sites.
finding: Most patients received appropriate antimicrobial prophylaxis for GBS and SSI prevention, but suboptimal use of second-line antibiotics for beta-lactam allergic patients and persistent issues with allergy documentation were identified.
